newsitem.title: USA: Exxon beats forecasts thanks to downstream.
newsitem.headline: Exxon beats forecasts thanks to downstream.

text.p: Exxon Corp beat even the most optimistic forecasts when it reported second quarter earnings per share rose to $0.79 from $0.63 a year ago due to surprisingly strong earnings at its U.S. downstream division.

Analysts had been looking for earnings per share of $0.71, according to First Call, although some had forecast that an upturn in overseas refining margins would lift the largest U.S. oil company to $0.75 per share in the quarter.

"We anticipated that lower crude oil prices would bolster refining margins, but this figure is much stronger than we had thought and the improvement was global," said Michael Young, at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, who had been at the top of analyst forecasts.

U.S. refining and marketing operations earnings rose to $162 million from $98.0 million, boosted by a strong performance on the Gulf Coast, the company said, whereas most analysts had been predicting a flat performance year-on-year.
This, and a rise in overseas refining and marketing earnings to $382 million from $134 million, more than offset the effect of a $1.50 per barrel decline in crude oil prices.

The overseas downstream was better than the expected $300 million in earnings and pushed total net income to $1.965 billion from $1.57 billion in the second quarter and to $4.14 billion for the first half, compared with $3.455 billion.
Refining margins improved in Europe, but were weaker in Asia-Pacific and there was some improvement in the UK, although a cutthroat retail price war meant that marketing margins remained weak.
"I think it would be a mistake to extrapollate out the improved dowsntream earnings for the full year," said Young.
Petroleum product sales rose six percent from a year ago 5.348 million barrels per day and refinery throughput rose 121,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 3.875 million.
Downstream year's second quarter. Sales volumes increased in all major geographic areas. Refinery throughput increased 121 kbd to 3,875 kbd reflecting lower scheduled maintenance.
Chemicals performance was also strong and second quarter chemical earnings rose to $246 million from $166 million in the U.S. and to $147 million from $138 million overseas.
This was in line with analyst forecasts.
"Chemicals improved lagely due to stronger prices for most commodity chemicals and somewhat lower feedstock costs," said a spokesman for the company.

Average oil prices in the U.S. fell to $15.31 per barrel from $17.07 and outside North America to $19.27 from $20.15, while natural gas prices dropped to $2.05 per thousand cubic feet from $2.23 in the United States.

The company said that production was also lower in the second quarter, at 1.588 million barrels per day (bpd) compared with 1.595 million a year ago due to maintenance, a revised production sharing agreement in Malaysia and field decline.
Natural gas production was 5.64 billion cubic feet per day, down from from 5.67 billion mcf a year ago.
Exxon's stock rose 14/16 by 1149 EDT to 61-5/16, having been as high as 62-1/8, volume was 1.752 million shares.
